seo.best_title: How Did Ancient Humans Go to the Toilet?
seo.description_hook: Right now you're sitting on something that used to be a death sentence. Here's how ancient humans actually went to the toilet.
paragraphs: For most of human history there was no toilet paper, no sewers, and no privacy. People used sticks, sponges on sticks, and even their hands. The results were often deadly.
Romans had public toilets with shared sponges. Medieval people threw waste out windows. The story is worse than you think.

shorts.title: Ancient Humans Had No Toilet Paper

shots.say: Right now you're sitting on something that used to be a death sentence.
For ten thousand years, almost nobody had toilet paper.
So what did they actually use?

scenes.say: Right now you're sitting on something that used to be a death sentence. For ten thousand years, almost nobody had toilet paper. So what did they actually use?

shots.say: Most people just used a stick.
Romans had a shared sponge on a stick in public toilets.
You wiped, rinsed it, and left it for the next person.
Which is wild when you think about it.

scenes.say: Most people just used a stick. Romans had a shared sponge on a stick in public toilets. You wiped, rinsed it, and left it for the next person. Which is wild when you think about it.

shots.say: The real problem wasn't the smell.
Bad sanitation caused more deaths than most wars.
We only fixed this a couple of centuries ago.
And that's why your toilet is actually one of the greatest inventions in history.
